title: Deprecate legacy button shim and introduce fluid state composition for icon & compound buttons
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Remove the legacy 'shim' wrapper used for historical button variants and replace it with a single fluid state composition architecture. Goals: simplify token mapping, unify loading/disabled behavior across text/icon/compound buttons, and fix a set of theme-dependent regressions surfaced in v2025.12. This ticket covers design decisions, token mappings, interaction specs, and acceptance criteria to hand off to engineering for implementation and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy shim removed; component API surface remains backward-compatible (deprecated props routed to new composition) and documented migration steps provided.
All button variants (primary/secondary/ghost/destructive/neutral) render identical focus/press/hover/disabled/loading affordances under light/dark/compact/expressive token scales.
Icon-only and compound (icon+label) buttons maintain consistent hit target and spinner placement without layout shift when toggling loading state.
Contrast ratios for focus ring and spinner meet WCAG AA for normal text (4.5:1) and an accessible fallback provided for low-contrast themes.
Automated visual regression snapshots show no unexpected diffs across token permutations, and existing failing snapshots are resolved.
Design handoff includes Figma prototypes, token diff table, and updated Storybook stories for QA and regression testing.
design_notes: Rationale: the legacy shim was a compatibility shim added in 2022 that layered ad-hoc overrides on top of tokens; it causes multiple code paths and visual regressions when introducing new tokens (e.g., spinner color under expressive themes).

Fluid state composition: model button as a stack of atomic states (base surface, icon layer, label layer, overlay indicators). State transitions use opacity/fade + transform (no layout reflow) to avoid visual jitter when showing spinner or switching to disabled.
Token mapping: produce a migration table mapping legacy CSS variables to new token names (surface-*, accent-*, border-*, spinner-*). Provide fallbacks for third-party theme overrides.

Hit targets: unify to 44px minimum touch target for compact and 48px for regular across icon-only and compound buttons. Use invisible padding token to preserve visual density while retaining hit area.

Spinner placement: centered for icon-only; trailing end (inline center-y) for compound buttons. Spinner should not cause text truncation; use overlay and preserve content width with absolute positioning.

Focus/press feedback: use a single focus ring token with adaptive thickness depending on density token (thin for compact, regular otherwise). Press states use a 6% scale darkening overlay with 120ms animation.
